newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha slips, LSWR done at 70 cts premium.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha slips, LSWR done at 70 cts premium.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices drifted lower on Friday, while one partial low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) cargo was traded at about 70 cents per barrel over the Pertamina formula, traders said.
"We fixed a small (LSWR) cargo at around a 70-cent premium to wrap up the June trading," one fuel oil trader said.
Indonesia has yet to announce its initial LSWR allocation for July lifting, traders said.
Open-spec naphtha for second-half August was assessed at $196.50/198.00 per tonne. It was said to have been traded several times in a range of $198 and $200 on Thursday.
First-half September was quoted at $197.50/199.50, compared with Thursday's $199.00/200.00.

Activity remained largely quiet in early afternoon trading, but traders were expected to come into the market later in the evening as most regional traders will leave their offices next Monday and Tuesday to attend the annual open-spec naphtha conference to be held in Tokyo, market participants said.

Naphtha term talks for Abu Dhabi cargoes have made little progress, a trader with one of the potential buyers said. The buying side held on to its bidding price of $20 per tonne over the ADNOC formula against Abu Dhabi's latest offer at $21.
